signals.title: EUR/USD — Macro Catalyst + Vol Premium + Retail Divergence
signals.text: EUR/USD trades at 1.1159, pinned below its SMA20 at 1.1327 and SMA50 at 1.1492 following a hot US September CPI print of 3.7% versus 3.6% expected. Fed policy rate at 4.00% (HIKING) versus ECB at 2.65% (HIKING) maintains a +135bp carry advantage favoring the dollar, with the OIS spread running +143bp. Options show ATM IV at 6.1% against HV30 of 4.0%, generating an elevated +2.2% vol risk premium that reflects sustained downside hedging demand rather than realized chop. Concurrently, retail positioning sits at an extreme 87% long, directly diverging from institutional COT leveraged funds holding net short -84,775 contracts (4th percentile of the 52-week range, z -1.64). This combination flags capitulation risk among retail longs as institutional momentum and rates reinforce the downward trajectory. Trade bias: Bearish EUR/USD; macro carry and spec short positioning dominate. Catalyst: Euro Area CPI final print on 15 Oct — 2.9% expected. Risk: Euro Area inflation accelerates sharply, forcing ECB terminal pricing higher and squeezing stretched institutional shorts.

signals.title: USD/JPY — Options Downside Skew + Technical Level
signals.text: USD/JPY prints at 158.33, holding below its daily SMA200 at 158.48 while remaining above the SMA20/50 cluster at 157.65/157.71. A +275bp policy rate gap (Fed 4.00% vs BoJ 1.25%) and a +264bp OIS carry advantage continue to support spot on dips. However, the 1-month 25d risk reversal reflects an extreme put skew at -1.70, showing market participants are aggressively bidding downside protection despite positive carry. Realized volatility sits at 9.7% against ATM IV of 7.6% (VRP -2.1%), highlighting options complacency in the face of elevated technical supply near the 160.00 psychological ceiling. A sustained push toward 160.00 elevates policy friction, where previous verbal warnings emerged. Trade bias: Neutral/range USD/JPY; wide carry cushioned by heavy options downside demand. Catalyst: BoJ meeting 30 Oct — hold expected. Risk: US yields advance further, pushing spot firmly through the SMA200 at 158.48 and exposing 160.00.

signals.title: NOK/EUR — G10 Bilateral Theme + Monetary Divergence
signals.text: The G10 Currency Strength Scorecard registers an active bilateral theme, with NOK leading at +0.741% across 2 pairs and EUR lagging at -0.387% across 9 pairs, generating a 1.128% spread. Norges Bank policy rate at 4.50% (HIKING) versus ECB at 2.65% (HIKING) provides a +185bp carry buffer that underpins relative outperformance. That rate differential is reinforced by a supportive economic surprise backdrop, where NOK ESI sits at +13.1 alongside firm front-month energy pricing with WTI crude holding at $95.10. Meanwhile, EUR sentiment suffers from German and Spanish unemployment beats adding domestic labor drag to ECB rate-pause expectations. Trade bias: Long NOK/EUR; rate spread and growth surprise gap favor trend extension. Catalyst: ECB meeting 29 Oct — hold bias priced. Risk: WTI crude drops sharply, undermining the terms-of-trade premium supporting NOK.

signals.title: AUD/USD — Event-Risk Compression + Technical Resistance
signals.text: AUD/USD trades at 0.6974, stationed below its SMA20 (0.7016), SMA50 (0.7089), and SMA200 (0.7040) resistance band. RBA policy rate at 4.60% (HIKING) versus Fed 4.00% (HIKING) yields a 60bp carry advantage in favor of AUD, matched by a -73bp OIS spread. CFTC data shows institutional leveraged funds hold net long positioning of +48,911 contracts (70.3% long), but momentum is decelerating after a WoW liquidation of -6,203 contracts. Intraday trading is compressed ahead of domestic employment data, with Australian unemployment forecast at 4.6% on a 14.0k headline employment gain. Trade bias: Neutral AUD/USD; carry advantage balanced by moving-average resistance overhead. Catalyst: Australia Employment Report at 00:30 UTC — 14.0K gain forecast. Risk: Australian employment posts a sharp upside surprise, pushing spot through the SMA200 at 0.7040.
